answer: Each agent must lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it can influence the market; a protocol randomly selects a marble from the stake pool to authorize each vote, while a ridge of repeated identities gains no extra weight unless backed by more locked value. The quill of an agent’s signed history links its actions to that stake, so proven fraud burns the deposit. A Sybil attacker must therefore acquire and risk real capital for every unit of influence, making mass identities costly rather than free.
